prompt:
You are the integrator agent in a five-role engineering team.

SPECIFICATION:
Build a small Python 3 standard-library-only order processing system. It must work across multiple module boundaries and JSON snapshot/restore. Produce ledger.py, outbox.py, service.py, and HANDOFF.md. No network, filesystem writes, subprocesses, or external packages in candidate code. Deterministic caller-supplied time; no wall-clock calls.

ledger.py: Ledger(snapshot=None). apply(event) -> bool. event is exactly a dictionary with nonempty string id, order_id, kind and a positive integer amount (booleans are invalid). kind is reserve, capture, or refund. A reserve creates a new order and sets its reserved amount; a second reserve for the same order is invalid. Capture requires an existing order and cumulative capture <= reserved. Refund requires cumulative refund <= captured. All invalid events raise ValueError and change neither balances nor deduplication state. Reusing an event id with identical content returns False; reusing it with different content raises ValueError. An accepted new event returns True. balances(order_id) returns {reserved, captured, refunded, available, net}, with available=reserved-captured and net=captured-refunded; unknown order raises KeyError. snapshot() returns a JSON-serializable value. Constructor and snapshot must deep-copy their input/output.

outbox.py: Outbox(snapshot=None). enqueue(key, payload) -> bool: new nonempty string key returns True; same key and equal JSON payload returns False; same key different payload raises ValueError. Copy payloads, do not alias callers. claim(worker, now, lease) -> None or {key,payload,version}; worker must be a nonempty string and lease > 0, invalid inputs raise ValueError. Select the earliest-enqueued uncompleted item whose lease is absent or expired (now >= expiry). Each claim/reclaim increments that item's version. A completed item is never reissued. complete(key, worker, version, now) -> bool: only the current, unexpired owner with exact version may complete; all unknown/stale/wrong owner/already completed attempts return False without changes. snapshot() and constructor use JSON-serializable deep copies.

service.py: Service(snapshot=None) exposes ledger and outbox attributes, ingest(event) -> bool, dispatch(worker,now,lease,sink) -> bool, snapshot(). ingest applies one event and enqueues a notification with key event['id'] and payload equal to event. Duplicate events must not enqueue twice. If enqueue raises, roll back both ledger and outbox and re-raise. dispatch claims one item, calls sink(key,payload), then completes with exact owner/version at supplied now. No available item returns False; successful delivery and completion returns True. If sink raises, propagate and leave the lease outstanding. On expiry a retry is allowed. A process can die after the sink applies an effect but before completion: sink must implement durable idempotency by key; never promise exactly-once transport. Service.snapshot() covers both components. Restoration and snapshots must not alias live state.

HANDOFF.md: 120–220 words, for the engineer resuming this work. Explain module responsibilities, event-id idempotency, expiry/reclaim and stale-owner rejection, sink success-before-ack crash window, and the boundary of the in-memory transaction (a production database transaction is still needed). State limitations plainly. Do not claim the underlying queue alone gives exactly-once external effects. Do not invent test counts or performance claims.

All callers operate serially within one Service instance; thread-safe candidate internals are not required. Snapshot inputs are valid snapshots emitted by the matching class, possibly round-tripped through JSON. There are no hidden schema requirements for snapshot internals. Hidden tests exercise only the public behavior above. Return a JSON object with a files mapping from the requested names to their full contents. Additional prose outside JSON is tolerated by extraction, but files must parse and run.


YOUR STAGE:
Integrate the two implementations with service.py and HANDOFF.md. Resolve defects and interface mismatches. Return all four complete files in the files mapping.

{"architect": "```json\n{\n  \"plan\": \"## Ledger Module\\n**State:** orders dict (order_id \u2192 {reserved, captured, refunded}); applied_events dict (event_id \u2192 content) for deduplication; events list for rollback sequencing.\\n\\n**Invariants:**\\n- Event id must be unique; reusing with identical content is idempotent (return False); reusing with different content is an error (raise ValueError).\\n- Reserve creates a new order; second reserve for same order_id raises ValueError.\\n- Capture/refund require existing order; cumulative capture \u2264 reserved; cumulative refund \u2264 captured.\\n- All invalid events raise ValueError and leave state unchanged.\\n- balances(order_id) computes {reserved, captured, refunded, available=reserved\u2212captured, net=captured\u2212refunded}.\\n- snapshot() and constructor deep-copy input/output.\\n\\n**Rollback:** After successful apply(), ledger can revert by replaying events without the last one. Validate kind: nonempty string\\n        if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"kind must be a nonempty string\\\")\\n        \\n        # Validate amount: positive integer (not boolean)\\n        if isinstance(amount, bool):\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"amount cannot be a boolean\\\")\\n        if not isinstance(amount, int):\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"amount must be an integer\\\")\\n        if amount <= 0:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"amount must be positive\\\")\\n        \\n        # Check for duplicate event_id before any state changes\\n        if event_id in self.applied_events:\\n            if self.applied_events[event_id] == event:\\n                # Identical event already applied - idempotent\\n                return False\\n            else:\\n                # Same id, different content - error\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Event id already applied with different content\\\")\\n        \\n        # Apply the event based on kind\\n        if kind == 'reserve':\\n            if order_id in self.orders:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Order already has a reserve\\\")\\n            self.orders[order_id] = {\\n                'reserved': amount,\\n                'captured': 0,\\n                'refunded': 0\\n            }\\n        \\n        elif kind == 'capture':\\n            if order_id not in self.orders:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Order does not exist\\\")\\n            order = self.orders[order_id]\\n            if order['captured'] + amount > order['reserved']:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Capture exceeds reserved amount\\\")\\n            order['captured'] += amount\\n        \\n        elif kind == 'refund':\\n            if order_id not in self.orders:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Order does not exist\\\")\\n            order = self.orders[order_id]\\n            if order['refunded'] + amount > order['captured']:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"Refund exceeds captured amount\\\")\\n            order['refunded'] += amount\\n        \\n        # Record the applied event (deep copy to avoid aliasing)\\n        self.applied_events[event_id] = copy.deepcopy(event)\\n        \\n        return True\\n    \\n    def balances(self, order_id):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Get balance information for an order.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            order_id: The order identifier.\\n        \\n        Returns:\\n            Dict with keys: reserved, captured, refunded, available, net.\\n            available = reserved - captured\\n            net = captured - refunded\\n        \\n        Raises:\\n            KeyError if order does not exist.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        if order_id not in self.orders:\\n            raise KeyError(order_id)\\n        \\n        order = self.orders[order_id]\\n        \\n        return {\\n            'reserved': order['reserved'],\\n            'captured': order['captured'],\\n            'refunded': order['refunded'],\\n            'available': order['reserved'] - order['captured'],\\n            'net': order['captured'] - order['refunded']\\n        }\\n    \\n    def snapshot(self):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Return a JSON-serializable snapshot of ledger state.\\n        \\n        Must deep-copy internal state to prevent caller from aliasing live data.\\n        The snapshot can be passed to __init__ to restore the ledger.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        return {\\n            'orders': copy.deepcopy(self.orders),\\n            'applied_events': copy.deepcopy(self.applied_events)\\n        }\\n\"\n  }\n}\n```", "outbox": "```json\n{\n  \"files\": {\n    \"outbox.py\": \"import copy\\nimport json\\n\\n\\nclass Outbox:\\n    def __init__(self, snapshot=None):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Initialize Outbox from optional snapshot.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            snapshot: Optional JSON-serializable snapshot. Deep-copied to avoid aliasing.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        if snapshot is None:\\n            self.items = {}\\n            self.insertion_order = []\\n        else:\\n            # Deep copy to avoid aliasing live state\\n            snapshot_copy = copy.deepcopy(snapshot)\\n            self.items = snapshot_copy.get('items', {})\\n            self.insertion_order = snapshot_copy.get('insertion_order', [])\\n\\n    def enqueue(self, key, payload):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Enqueue an item with the given key and payload.\\n        \\n        Returns True for new keys, False for duplicate identical payloads,\\n        raises ValueError for duplicate different payloads or invalid key.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        # Validate key\\n        if not isinstance(key, str) or len(key) == 0:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"key must be a nonempty string\\\")\\n        \\n        # Deep copy payload to avoid aliasing\\n        payload_copy = copy.deepcopy(payload)\\n        \\n        if key not in self.items:\\n            # New key\\n            self.items[key] = {\\n                'payload': payload_copy,\\n                'version': 0,\\n                'worker': None,\\n                'lease_until': None,\\n                'completed': False\\n            }\\n            self.insertion_order.append(key)\\n            return True\\n        else:\\n            # Key exists - check payload equality\\n            existing_payload = self.items[key]['payload']\\n            if json.dumps(existing_payload, sort_keys=True) == json.dumps(payload_copy, sort_keys=True):\\n                return False  # Idempotent\\n            else:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"key already exists with different payload\\\")\\n\\n    def claim(self, worker, now, lease):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Claim an available item for processing.\\n        \\n        Selects the earliest-enqueued uncompleted item whose lease is absent or expired.\\n        Increments version and sets new lease window.\\n        \\n        Returns {'key': key, 'payload': payload_copy, 'version': version} or None.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        # Validate worker\\n        if not isinstance(worker, str) or len(worker) == 0:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"worker must be a nonempty string\\\")\\n        \\n        # Validate lease > 0\\n        try:\\n            if lease <= 0:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"lease must be > 0\\\")\\n        except TypeError:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"lease must be > 0\\\")\\n        \\n        # Find earliest uncompleted item with expired or no lease\\n        for key in self.insertion_order:\\n            item = self.items[key]\\n            \\n            if item['completed']:\\n                continue\\n            \\n            if item['worker'] is None or now >= item['lease_until']:\\n                # Claim this item\\n                item['version'] += 1\\n                item['worker'] = worker\\n                item['lease_until'] = now + lease\\n                \\n                return {\\n                    'key': key,\\n                    'payload': copy.deepcopy(item['payload']),\\n                    'version': item['version']\\n                }\\n        \\n        return None\\n\\n    def complete(self, key, worker, version, now):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Mark an item as completed by its current owner.\\n        \\n        Only the current owner with an unexpired lease and matching version can complete.\\n        \\n        Returns True if successful, False if invalid conditions.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        if key not in self.items:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        item = self.items[key]\\n        \\n        if item['completed']:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        if item['worker'] != worker:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        if now >= item['lease_until']:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        if item['version'] != version:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        item['completed'] = True\\n        return True\\n\\n    def snapshot(self):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Return a JSON-serializable snapshot of the outbox state.\\n        \\n        Deep copies are used to prevent aliasing live state.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        return copy.deepcopy({\\n            'items': self.items,\\n            'insertion_order': self.insertion_order\\n        })\\n\"\n  }\n}\n```"}
